verses.1: For every high priest, as he was chosen from among men, he held himself in accordance with God’s will, so that he might offer gifts and sacrifices for the sins of people.
verses.2: Being able to endure those who are ignorant and deluded, even since he himself also suffers from a disease.
verses.3: And because of her, he also owes her something, just as he owes the people for their sins.
verses.4: And no one receives honor for himself alone; rather, he is honored by God, just as Aaron was.
verses.5: Similarly, Christ also did not consider himself worthy of being an archbishop. Instead, he said to him, “You are my son; I have now given you birth.”
verses.6: And in another place he says: “You, priest, go into the wilderness according to the order of Melchizedek.”
verses.7: Whoever in those days demands both help and support from those who are capable of saving him from death, by crying out loudly and with tears in his eyes.
verses.8: And as a son, he learned from his father how to endure hardship.
verses.9: And when it was completed, it became a cause of eternal salvation for all who obeyed it.
verses.10: The high priest, appointed by God, was Melchizedek.
verses.11: Regarding this, it’s difficult for us to speak about it in a way that isn’t confusing. After all, you’ve become deaf to what we say.
verses.12: And since teachers are indeed owed their wages over time, it is still necessary for them to teach you the principles of God’s laws. You also need milk; it’s not a thing that can be easily replaced by anything else.
verses.13: For every person who consumes milk, there’s a vast amount of reasoning related to justice involved. After all, it’s still just a childish matter.
verses.14: In conclusion, the true nourishment is that which enables the senses to distinguish between good and bad things.
